title: Noor and the Ledger
premise: Retired detective Kestrel Ravensworth, now barely keeping his bookshop afloat, is handed the diary of Noor Adeyemi, a young woman who vanished eleven years ago in a case ruled a runaway. The diary's final entries are dated after her disappearance, written in a hand that isn't hers, and they name three men whose alibis were quietly stitched together thirty years earlier by a powerful local family. As Kestrel reopens the threads, he discovers Noor may still be alive, hidden by choice, and that the 'missing person' case was manufactured to bury what she witnessed as a child. At trial, Kestrel chooses to protect Noor's anonymity rather than win the conviction cleanly, letting the ledger of evidence destroy the family's power while justice arrives outside the verdict.
about_author: Ulyana Oyelaran is a former court archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cold-case files before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who refuse to let official records have the last word.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A lawyer friend leaves Noor Adeyemi's recovered diary on the bookshop counter; its last entries postdate her disappearance and shift handwriting mid-sentence. Kestrel, restless since retirement, begins reading against his better judgment. Emotional beat: the thrill of purpose returning, shadowed by dread that this case will cost him more than the last three.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He maps the deaths the police closed as accidents and finds each victim connected to the Voss family's old shipping empire. Flashback fragments reveal how, thirty years ago, a single night at Voss House bound four witnesses into one alibi. Emotional beat: quiet fury at how neatly power erases itself from paper.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Regulars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Marisol, a teenage shop assistant who has become Kestrel's unlikely protégée. She notices him pulling old case files and, instead of asking questions, starts covering his shifts. Emotional beat: warmth and found family — the first hint that Kestrel won't face this alone, whether he wants help or not.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He tracks down two of the original alibi witnesses: one dead, one dying, who confesses the alibi was rehearsed by the family's fixer. The dying man gives Kestrel a name — the child who saw everything that night was never found. Emotional beat: grief for complicity, and the first hard evidence that the past was constructed, not remembered.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. While Kestrel sleeps, she studies the diary's late entries and realizes the second handwriting belongs to someone protecting Noor — someone writing to keep the file alive. She decodes a recurring reference to a lighthouse on the coast. Emotional beat: Marisol stepping from helper to investigator, terrified and exhilarated.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He breaks into the estate office of the retired fixer, Edmund Voss's former solicitor, and finds a literal ledger: payments, threats, and a standing annual sum labeled only 'N.A.' — still being paid today. Emotional beat: vertigo. If the payments continue, Noor may be alive, and every year of silence was purchased.

chapters.title: What the Family Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Voss heir, Celia, learns someone is asking about the ledger and orders surveillance on the bookshop. Her chapters reveal she inherited the cover-up without believing in it — until she reads her father's letters. Emotional beat: Celia's corruption curdling into panic; the antagonist becomes human and more dangerous for it.

chapters.title: Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Marisol's POV, alternating. Following the diary clue, they find Noor living under another name, unbroken but imprisoned by fear. She refuses to testify; the trial looms regardless, built on Kestrel's leaked evidence. Emotional beat: the moral crux — Kestrel must choose between the verdict he's chased and the woman it would destroy.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In court, the prosecution's case wobbles as the defense dismantles chain of custody. Kestrel holds back the one piece that identifies where Noor is, watching Celia realize he's withholding. A threat against Marisol forces his hand toward a reckless move outside the law. Emotional beat: rising dread; the system failing exactly as Noor predicted.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Kestrel releases the ledger publicly through the bookshop's network of readers, letting the town — not the court — render judgment; the Voss name collapses, Celia cooperates to save herself, and Noor testifies on her own terms, anonymously. The bookshop survives, fuller than before. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — imperfect justice, but a family found and a record finally true.
